title.narrative: Social Care and Dementia Support to Jewish Communities

description.narrative: The aim of this project is to improve the quality of life of older people living with dementia who are isolated from community life and lack specialist services. The project will also build support networks for those caring for a relative with dementia, increase awareness about dementia to build a more tolerant, dementia-friendly community. Lastly it aims to increase social contact for isolated people living alone by providing befriending services, and provide medical assistance to people on low pensions without family support. World Jewish Relief has been working in Belarus since the 1990s in partnership with the local Belarusian organisation Hesed Rakhamim which supports over 2,000 older Jewish people in Minsk who require medical and social support. Between October 2024 and March 2025, this project will reach around 64 people directly with dementia and befriending services, and over 100 people with access to training and guidance. It will provide tailored support and socialisation for beneficiaries, depending on their needs, including befriending and activities to stimulate memory and maintain communication skills. Activities will be either in person at home, at a day centre, or online depending on the beneficiariesâ€™ capabilities. Finally, the project will run training to raise awareness of person-centred care, upskilling carers who assist those living with dementia, and build the capacity of other organisations that serve the Belarusian Jewish community to provide similar activities and care.
